ES5H: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the grace of the True Guru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God, By the True Guru's grace, He is obtained.
6E7W: Raag Bilaval, Ghar 11: a Bani of eight-stanza hymns by Guru Ram Das ji.
Bilaaval, Fourth Mehl, Ashtpadheeyaa, Eleventh House:
DX05: Aapai = into Parmatma's own self. Aap = one's own self. Khai = consuming, ending. Hau = ego. Andin = every day, at every moment {anudinam}. Har ras geet = songs of the nectar of Hari's Name.
O brother! The person who keeps singing songs of the nectar of Hari's Name at every moment merges their own self into (Parmatma's) self and wipes out ego (from within).
One who eliminates his self-centeredness, and eradicates his ego, night and day sings the songs of the Lord's Love.
He, who effaces his self and eradicates his ego, Night and day sings the songs of the Lord's love.
O brother! Whoever wipes out ego and, day and night, always sings Hari's songs with (ras) love — then they themselves (khai) taste, that is, experience, the bliss of their own true form.
UR6F: Gurmukh = taking the Guru's shelter. Parchai = is absorbed, is won over. Kanchan = gold, pure as gold. Kaia = body. Joti = into Parmatma's light. Jot = the soul. ||1||
The person who, taking the Guru's shelter, stays absorbed (in Hari's Name) — (kept from vices) their body becomes pure as gold. Their soul stays merged in the light of fearless Prabhu. ||1||
The Gurmukh is inspired, his body is golden, and his light merges into the Light of the Fearless Lord. ||1||
The body of him, who is sated by Guru's grace, becomes pure like gold and his light merges in the Supreme light of the Fear-Free. Lord.

In this way, those who are absorbed in the Name through the Guru — their (kaia) understanding has become pure like gold, and they have become fearless. So their light has merged into (joti) Vahiguru. ||1|| ☬ The ending at the close of every line marks a particular form, or is a rhyme.
DL6L: Aadhar = support. Naam ramaeea = the Name of the beautiful Ram.
O brother! The Name of the beautiful Ram has become the support (of my life) for me.
I take the Support of the Name of the Lord, Har, Har.
I have the support of the Name of the Omnipresent Lord God,
Hari, the remover of suffering, whose form (ramaeea) pervades all — I have taken the support of His Name, Hari.
816G: Reh na sakau = I cannot live. ||1|| Rahau ||
(Now) I cannot live even an instant or a moment without His Name. Taking the Guru's shelter, (I) keep reading the recitation of Hari's Name. ||1|| Rahau ||
I cannot live, for a moment, even for an instant, without the Name of the Lord; the Gurmukh reads the Sermon of the Lord, Har, Har. ||1||Pause||
Even for a moment and a trice I can live not without the Name and by Guru's grace read I the Lord God's discourse. Pause.
Now I cannot live even for an instant or a moment without that Name, and through the Guru I have read the recitation of the Name Har Har. ||1|| Rahau ||
LX9P: Girahu = home, (the body-)house. Duar = doors. Ja ke = whose (body-house). Ahi = day. Nis = night. Taskar = thieves. Panch chor = the five thieves (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride).
O brother! (This human body) is a house with ten doors; (through these doors) the five thieves (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) keep breaking in day and night.
In the one house of the body, there are ten gates; night and day, the five thieves break in.
There is one body-house, which has ten doors, the five thieves and burglars, day and night break into it.
There is one house, the body, whose ten doors are the ten senses. Day and night, lust, anger and the other five stay after that house like thieves out to steal.
DPAW: Arath = wealth. Sabh = all. Hir le javah = steal away. Manmukh = one who follows their own mind. Andhule = (spiritually) blind. ||2||
They steal away all the wealth of spiritual life (from within it). The self-willed person, (spiritually) blind, does not even notice (that they are being robbed). ||2||
They steal the entire wealth of one's Dharmic faith, but the blind, self-willed manmukh does not know it. ||2||
They steal the entire wealth of righteousness, but the blind apostate knows it not.
Those thieves (hir) steal away its (arath) wealth, which is dharma — or the four fruits: dharma, wealth and the rest — but the ignorant, self-willed being notices nothing. ||2||
JHQG: Kanchan kot = a fortress of gold. Manak = with rubies, with high spiritual virtues. Jage = those who stayed awake, stayed alert. Tat = in the essence. Giaan tat = in the essence of spiritual life. Liv laeea = fixing attention.

O brother! (This human body is, as it were,) a fortress of gold filled with the pearls (of high spiritual virtues). Those who stay alert, fixing their attention on Prabhu, the source of spiritual life, (save their spiritual wealth).
The fortress of the body is overflowing with gold and jewels; when it is awakened by spiritual wisdom, one enshrines love for the essence of reality.
The body-fortress is brimful with gold and gems, When Divine wisdom awakens into it, man comes to enshrine love for reality.

And the fortress of gold is this subtle body — that is, priceless and hard to come by. It is filled with rubies, the good virtues such as reflection. Those who have woken, in this fortress, into the wakefulness of knowledge have fixed their attention on that essence of consciousness.
W29H: Taskar = thieves. Heru = robbers. Kai sabad = through the Word of. Pakar = catching. Bandh paeea = tied up. ||3||
Thieves and robbers (lust and the rest) come and hide (in it, to steal and loot these jewels). Those (alert) people catch (these thieves and robbers) through the Guru's Word and tie them up. ||3||
The thieves and robbers hide out in the body; through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, they are arrested and locked up. ||3||
The thieves and snatchers are hid in the body. By means of Guru's hymns, he arrests and binds them down.

Lust, anger and the other thieves, (heru) out to carry off or spy on the wealth of dharma, had come and hidden in the body. Through the True Guru's Word those thieves have been caught and bound — meaning lust, anger and the other vices have gone. ||3||
HRPA: Pot = ship. Bohitha = ship. Khevat = boatman.

O brother! Parmatma's Name is a ship, a great ship; (the Guru's) Word is the boatman (of that ship); (the person who takes the support of this ship,) the Guru carries across (the world-ocean full of vices).
The Name of the Lord, Har, Har, is the boat, and the Word of the Guru's Shabad is the boatman, to carry us across.
The Lord God's Name is the boat and ship and the Guru's word the boatman, through whom the mortal crosses the world-ocean.

Hari's Name alone is the (pot) treasure of all comforts; Hari's Name alone is the (bohitha) ship that carries one across the world-ocean. The True Guru, who is the (khevat) boatman, gives His (sabad) teaching and carries one across that ocean.
TN7X: Jagati = toll-collector. Ko taskar = any thief. Lagaeea = breaks in. ||4||
Yama the toll-collector does not come near (them either), and no thief (such as lust) can break in. ||4||
The Messenger of Death, the tax collector, does not even come close, and no thieves or robbers can plunder you. ||4||
Death's courier, the tax-gatherer, comes not near the Guru's slave and no burglar or thief thieves.
And the toll-collector, Yama, does not come near them, nor does any robber thief such as lust or anger touch them again. ||4||
MYJK: Gavai = is singing. Jas = praise. Kahte = while telling. Ant = the limit of His praises.
O brother! (My mind now) keeps singing Parmatma's virtues always, day and night; praising Prabhu again and again, I cannot find the end (of His praise).
I continuously sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord, day and night; singing the Lord's Praises, I cannot find His limits.
Day and night I ever sing God's virtues. Uttering the Lord's praises, I find not His limit.
We sing such virtues of Hari always, day and night, but telling Hari's praise I have not found its end — meaning His praise is endless.
TTKZ: Gurmukh = taking the Guru's shelter. Ikat = in the one. Ghar = in the home. Ikat ghar = in the one home, at Prabhu's feet alone. Aavai = comes. Milau = I am meeting. Gopal = {the letter 'g' carries two vowel signs; the actual word is 'Gopal', to be read here as 'Gupal'}. Neesan bajaeea = sounding the drum, without hesitation, casting off shyness. ||5||
Taking the Guru's shelter, (this) mind (of mine) stays settled at Prabhu's feet alone; casting off what people may say, I stay united with the Sustainer of the world. ||5||
The mind of the Gurmukh returns to its own home; it meets the Lord of the Universe, to the beat of the celestial drum. ||5||
By Guru's grace, the mind comes into its one Home and then it meets with the World Cherisher, with the beat of drum.
When, taking the teaching through the Guru, my mind comes into that home of one-pointedness, then, beating the (neesan) drum of speaking the Name, may I meet that Gopal. ||5||
6M4U: Naini = with the eyes. Dekh = seeing. Tripatai = stays satisfied (free of other desires). Sravan = ears.
O brother! Seeing (Prabhu everywhere) with (my) eyes, (my) mind stays satisfied (free of other desires); (my) ears keep hearing the Guru's Bani, the Guru's Word.
Gazing upon the Blessed Vision of His Darshan with my eyes, my mind is satisfied; with my ears, I listen to the Guru's Bani, and the Word of His Shabad.
Seeing the Lord's vision with my eyes my soul is sated and with my ears, hear I the Guru's hymns and instruction.
Seeing the True Guru's sight with my eyes, may my mind be satisfied, and may I listen with my ears to the Bani that is the Guru's Word.
JCK1: Sun = hearing. Aatam dev = the soul, the life. Hai bheene = stays soaked. Ras = with delight. Ras ras = with great delight. Ravaeea = remembers. ||6||
Hearing and hearing (Prabhu's praise), (my) soul stays soaked (in the nectar of the Name); (I) keep singing the virtues of Ram-Gopal with great bliss. ||6||
Listening, listening, my soul is softened, delighted by His subtle essence, chanting the Name of the Lord of the Universe. ||6||
Continually hearing the Guru's word, the human soul is softened and delighted with the Lord's elixir and utters the Master's Name.
Hearing and hearing that Guru's Bani, we are soaked in the divine self. By that, (ras) in love, becoming (ras) one with Him, we delight always in Gopal, whose form (Ram) pervades all. ||6||
JN10: Trai gun = the three qualities (of Maya: rajas, sattva, tamas), the beings who live under the sway of these three. Moh = in attachment. Viape = caught. Turia gun = the spiritual state where the three qualities of Maya have no sway, the fourth state. Gurmukh = the one who stays facing the Guru.

O brother! Beings who live under the sway of Maya's three qualities stay (always) caught in attachment to Maya. The one who stays facing the Guru reaches the fourth state (where Maya can have no sway).
In the grip of the three qualities, they are engrossed in love and attachment to Maya; only as Gurmukh do they find the absolute quality, absorption in bliss.
Men of three qualities are engrossed in the love of mammon. It is through the Guru, that man attains to the supreme status.
All beings of the three qualities are caught in the attachment of Maya; the (turia) fourth quality, the state of the self, has been (laheeaa) reached by the Gurmukhs alone.
V9S5: Sabh = all people. Sam = equal, the same. Jaanai = knows. Nadri aavai = is seen. Sabh = everywhere. Pasraeea = spread out. ||7||
(The one who stays facing the Guru) looks with one (loving) gaze and knows all people as the same. They see (it plainly) that Parmatma alone is spread out everywhere. ||7||
With a single, impartial eye, look upon all alike, and see God pervading all. ||7||
With the same one eye, he deems all alike and sees the Supreme Lord pervading all.
With the gaze of oneness they know all as equal. In all the expanse they (nadri) see the one form of Brahm spread out. ||7||
SP37: Sabaee = all creation. Gurmukh lakhaeea = the one who stays facing the Guru understands. Aape = Himself. Alakh = the Parmatma whose true form cannot be grasped.
O brother! The one who stays facing the Guru understands that the unseen Prabhu is Himself (present everywhere); everywhere is Parmatma's Name alone, and in all people is Parmatma's light alone.
The Light of the Lord's Name permeates all; the Gurmukh knows the unknowable.
The light of the Lord's Name is permeating all, The Guru-ward automatically comes to perceive the unperceivable.
The light of Vahiguru, whose Name is Ram, has come into all. Knowing Him as their own self, the Gurmukhs have seen that unseen form.
M3B3: Bhagat bhai = with the feeling of devotion {bhau = love; bhai = through love}. Naam = in the Name. ||8||1||4||
O Nanak! Those on whom Prabhu ji, merciful to the humble, is merciful stay merged in Parmatma's Name through the feeling of devotion. ||8||1||4||
O Nanak, the Lord has become merciful to the meek; through loving adoration, he merges in the Lord's Name. ||8||1||4||
God has become merciful to meek Nanak, who through His living adoration has been absorbed in His Name.

Sri Guru ji says: whoever has become humble before Vahiguru — that Hari has been merciful to them. That person, through loving devotion, has merged into that (naam) Vahiguru. ||8||1||4|| ☬ Showing what he has gained from the Name, he teaches the devotees, with proofs:
GGL7: Seetal = cooling. Dhiavahu = remember. Vaas = fragrance. Gandhaeea = makes fragrant.
O brother! Remember Prabhu's Name; this Name is cooling water; this Name is the fragrance of sandalwood that makes (all the vegetation) fragrant.
Meditate on the cool water of the Name of the Lord, Har, Har. Perfume yourself with the fragrant scent of the Lord, the sandalwood tree.
Contemplate you the cool water like Name, of the Lord God. One is perfumed with the scent and fragrance of God, the sandal.

The Name Har Har is the water that cools the heart. O brother! Meditate on that alone. And Hari is the sandalwood with the finest (gandhaeea) fragrance of all; take His sweet fragrance — or the good praise of devotion.

8JP0: Mil = joining. Param pad = the highest spiritual state. Hirad = the castor plant. Palas = the palas tree. Sang = with (sandalwood). Buheeaa = becomes fragrant. ||1||

O brother! Joining the holy company, one gains the highest spiritual state. Just as the castor and palas (and other worthless trees become fragrant in the company of sandalwood), (so) beings like me (become of high character through the blessing of Hari's Name). ||1||
Joining the Society of the Saints, I have obtained the supreme status. I am just a castor-oil tree, made fragrant by their association. ||1||
Joining the society of saints, I have obtained the supreme status. Meeting with God, I who was like the castor-oil plant and buteafrondosa tree, have become sweetly scented.

Joining the true company, I have gained the highest state. Although I was worthless like the castor plant and the (palas) dhak tree, joining Hari the sandalwood I have become (buheeaa) fragrant — that is, full of praise. ||1||
TXWU: Jap = keep chanting. Jagannath = Master of the world. Jagdees = Ishvar of the world. Gusaeea = Master of the earth.
O brother! Keep chanting the Name of Prabhu, Master of the world, Ishvar of the world, Master of the earth.
Meditate on the Lord of the Universe, the Master of the world, the Lord of creation.
O man, remember you the Lord of the universe, the Master of the world and the Proprietor of creation.
O brother! Remember with mind, body and speech the Name of Vahiguru — Master of the world, Ishvar of all, (gusaeea) the Master of the earth.
CP3U: Ubre = saved from vices. Udhar = carrying across. ||1|| Rahau ||
Those who come to Prabhu's shelter escape (from the world-ocean), just as (Parmatma) carried Prahlad (and other devotees) across (the world-ocean) and merged them (at His feet). ||1|| Rahau ||
Those humble beings who seek the Lord's Sanctuary are saved, like Prahlaad; they are emancipated and merge with the Lord. ||1||Pause||
They who seek the Lord's protection; those persons are saved like Prahlad. They are emancipated and merged in the Lord. Pause.

Those who have fallen at His shelter are the people who have been (ubre) saved from the sufferings of this world. How? Just as He (udhar) pulled Prahlad out of suffering and merged him into His own form. ||1|| Rahau ||
YRZ7: Bhar atharah = all vegetation. {An old idea has come down that taking one leaf from every plant and weighing them would come to 18 bhar. One bhar is five kachcha maunds.} Nikat = near.
O brother! In all vegetation sandalwood is the finest (tree); every plant (growing) near sandalwood becomes sandalwood.
Of all plants, the sandalwood tree is the most sublime. Everything near the sandalwood tree becomes fragrant like sandalwood.
In the entire vegetation, the sandal tree is the most sublime. All that is near the sandal tree becomes fragrant like sandal.

All vegetation is called "eighteen bhar". It is like this: 3,260 tolas are called one bhar. Taking one leaf from each kind of tree and weighing them together makes eighteen such bhar — that much vegetation there is. He gives an illustration: in all that eighteen bhar of vegetation, sandalwood alone is the finest, because the trees near sandalwood — all except bamboo — become sandalwood themselves. In the same way, in the whole world of name and form, the saints are supremely fine like sandalwood. Those who keep the saints' company become their very form.
WXP2: Saakat = people cut off from Parmatma. Oobh suk = trees dried up while still standing (on the ground). Man = in the mind. Vichhurr = being separated. ||2||

But beings cut off from Parmatma and wrapped in Maya (are like trees that) dry up while still standing (even though they can draw food from the earth); pride lives in (their) mind, (so) separated (from Parmatma) they stay somewhere far away. ||2||
The stubborn, false faithless cynics are dried up; their egotistical pride separates them far from the Lord. ||2||
The stiff-necked and false mammon-worshippers are dried up. Their mind's ego separates them far from the Lord.

Those who have turned away are like trees dried up where they stand, empty of the greenness that is all virtues — meaning they are impure and hard. They do not become sandalwood; they are fit only to be burnt in hells. Through pride in their mind they have been separated from Vahiguru and gone far away — meaning those people wander through the 84 lakh births. ||2||
TL5J: Gat = high spiritual state. Mit = count, bounds, limit. Aape = Himself. Sabh bidh = the whole order.

O brother! What Parmatma is like and how great He is — He Himself knows. He Himself has made the whole order (of the world); (by that order) the person who meets the Guru becomes gold (turns to a pure life).
Only the Creator Lord Himself knows the state and condition of everyone; the Lord Himself makes all the arrangements.
The Lord creator Himself knows the condition and life's department of everyone, All the arrangements the Lord God Himself makes.
That Hari, the Creator, Himself knows the state and the (mit) bounds of all beings, because that Hari Himself has made the order of the whole world in every way.
GLWK: Bhete = meets. Kanchan = gold. Dhur = from the court on high. ||3||

O brother! (The record) written from the court on high (on beings' foreheads, according to their deeds) cannot be erased (by anyone's own effort) (only by meeting the Guru does iron become gold). ||3||
One who meets the True Guru is transformed into gold. Whatever is pre-ordained, is not erased by erasing. ||3||
He, whom the True Guru meets is transformed into gold. What ever is pre-ordained, that can be erased not by erasing.
The person who meets the True Guru becomes pure like gold. The record Vahiguru wrote from the (dhur) beginning cannot be erased by anyone. ||3||
WNHF: Gurmat = through the Guru's teaching. Paavai = (a person) finds. Saagar = ocean.
O brother! (Within the Guru) oceans of devotion (lie full); treasures of devotion lie open; only by walking by the Guru's teaching can a person gain the jewels (of high spiritual virtues).
The treasure of jewels is found in the ocean of the Guru's Teachings. The treasure of devotional worship is opened to me.
In the ocean of the Guru's instruction, find I the jewel like wealth of the Lord's Name and the treasure of His meditation is opened to me.
In the world-ocean, the (bhandar) treasure of devotion that is the true company lies open; but a being gains the (ratan) jewels such as detachment through the Guru's (mat) teaching.
CPTL: Ik sardha = love for the One Parmatma. Kahte = while telling. Tripat = fulfilment. ||4||
(See:) by falling at the Guru's feet, love for the One Parmatma has arisen (in me); (now) my mind is never full of singing Parmatma's virtues. ||4||
Focused on the Guru's Feet, faith wells up within me; chanting the Glorious Praises of the Lord, I hunger for more. ||4||
Adoring Guru's feet, faith has welled up in me, Uttering the Lord's praise my hunger for it is appeased not.
From the feet of that True Guru one faith has arisen in me: that I am never satisfied while speaking Hari's virtues. ||4||
3ANR: Param bairag = the highest detachment, the deepest longing. Bhavni = love.
O brother! The person who keeps meditating on Parmatma always comes to have the deepest longing within. I have told (you of) the love that has formed in me while singing and singing Prabhu's virtues.
I am totally detached, continually, continuously meditating on the Lord; chanting the Glorious Praises of the Lord, I express my love for Him.
Ever, ever on contemplating my Lord, ever contemplating on my Lord, supreme detachedness has welled up in me. I express my love by uttering God's praise love.

Those who, supremely detached, have meditated on Hari always, every day — the saints who speak Hari's virtues — the Guru has given me (bhavni) faith in them; or, speaking Hari's virtues, (mai hiaa) my heart has become (bhavni) beautiful.
NC4R: Baar baar = again and again. Kaheeai = should be remembered. Paar = the far shore. Parai paraeea = beyond the beyond. ||5||
So, O brother! Parmatma's Name should be chanted again and again, every instant, every moment (but remember this): Parmatma is beyond the beyond; no being can find the far shore of His (being). ||5||
Time and time again, each and every moment and instant, I express it. I cannot find the Lord's limits; He is the farthest of the far. ||5||
Uttering His praise over and over again and every moment and trice, one can find not God's limit. He is the remotest of the remote.

Even if we speak Hari's Name again and again, every instant and every moment, no one finds the end of Hari's virtues, because that Hari is beyond all — endless even beyond Brahma and the others, who are beyond everything. ||5||
55YA: Pukarah = cry out, (stress this very point). Dharam = (the six-deed) dharma. Khat karam = the six religious duties (studying and teaching, performing and having performed sacrifices, giving and receiving charity). Drirraeea = they insist.
O brother! The Vedas, Shastras and Puranas (and other religious books) stress (this very point): practise (the six-deed) dharma; they insist on these six religious duties.
The Shaastras, the Vedas and the Puraanas advise righteous actions, and the performance of the six religious rituals.
The Shastras, the Vedas and the Puranas proclaim the doing of good deeds and steadfastly performing the six religious rites.

The six Shastras, the eighteen Puranas and the four Vedas cry out: "O brother! Practise dharma, and fix firmly in your mind the six duties: 1 chanting, 2 fire-offering, 3 the evening prayer, 4 bathing, 5 worship of the gods, 6 honouring guests."
DSLY: Manmukh = people who follow their own mind. Pakhand = in hypocrisy. Bharam = in wandering. Vigoote = are ruined. Naav = the boat (of life). Bhar = by the weight. ||6||
People who follow their own mind are ruined in (this very) hypocrisy and wandering; the boat (of their life) sinks in the wave of greed under the weight (of their own hypocrisy). ||6||
The hypocritical, self-willed manmukhs are ruined by doubt; in the waves of greed, their boat is heavily loaded, and it sinks. ||6||
The perverse hypocrites rites. The perverse hypocrites are ruined in doubt. Their boat is heavily Loaded with sins and sinks in the tides of avarice contemplate.
But self-willed, hypocritical people are ruined by doubt; in the wave of greed, under the weight of sins, the (naav) boat of their understanding has (budaeea) sunk. ||6||
00H5: Naame = through the Name alone. Gat = high spiritual state. Drirraeea = make firm in the heart.

O brother! Keep chanting Parmatma's Name; only by joining with the Name will you reach the high spiritual state. Keep (Parmatma's) Name firmly settled (in your heart); (for the one who faces the Guru, this Name of Hari alone) is the teaching of the Smritis and Shastras.
So chant the Naam, the Name of the Lord, and through the Naam, find emancipation. The Simritees and Shaastras recommend the Naam.
You the Name and through the Name be blessed with emancipation. The Simirtis and Shashtras impress the Name's meditation.
So, O brother! Chant the Name of that Vahiguru. Through that Name alone you will gain (gat) well-being; the Shastras and Smritis all make the Name firm.
W438: Jai = goes. Ta = then. Nirmal = of pure life. Gurmukh = through the Guru. Parchai = is absorbed (in the Name). Param pad = the highest spiritual state. ||7||

(When, through Hari's Name,) ego goes (from within), then a person comes to live a pure life. When, taking the Guru's shelter, a person is won over (by Parmatma's Name), then they reach the highest spiritual state. ||7||
Eradicating egotism, one becomes pure. The Gurmukh is inspired, and obtains the supreme status. ||7||
If man stills his ego and by Guru's grace imbibes Lord's love, then he becomes pure and obtains the supreme status.

When this being's dirt of ego goes, then they become pure. And when, taking the teaching through the Guru, they are absorbed in that Vahiguru's Name, then they reach the highest state. ||7|| ☬ So, O brother, pray like this before that Vahiguru:
C19Y: Varan = colour. Jit = in which (work). Laavah = You attach. Se = those {plural}.
(O Prabhu!) This whole world is Your form alone, Your colour alone. Wherever You attach (beings), those are the deeds beings do.
This world, with its colors and forms, is all Yours, O Lord; as You attach us, so do we do our deeds.
O Lord, this world, with all the colours and forms, is Yours. To what-so-ever You attachest men, those deeds do they do.
This world — the (varan) castes such as Brahmin and Kshatriya, and all (roop) forms — is all Your doing. Wherever You direct these beings, those deeds they (kamaeea) do.
MHHZ: Jant = beings {plural}. Vaajah = sound. Jit = on which (path). Bhavai = pleases You. Tit raah = on that path. ||8||2||5||
O Nanak! (Say:) beings (are Your instruments); they sound as You play them. Whatever path pleases You to set them on, on that path beings walk. ||8||2||5||
O Nanak, we are the instruments upon which He plays; as He wills, so is the path we take. ||8||2||5||
Nanak, the mortals are the instruments in the Lord's hands and play as He makes them play. As He wills, that path tread on they.

Sri Guru ji says: just as all instruments sound as the player plays them, so, O Hari, on whatever path pleases You, on that path these beings (chalaeea) walk. Meaning, these beings are not free; they are wholly in Your hands — so You Yourself show them grace. ||8||2||5|| ☬ Again, showing his own state, he teaches:
27Q8: Gurmukh = through the Guru, taking the Guru's shelter. Agam = unreachable. Agochar = {a-go-char; go = the senses} beyond the reach of the senses. Hau = I. Bal bal = a sacrifice.
O brother! I am a sacrifice, again and again, to the Guru, the great Being. Taking the Guru's shelter, I keep remembering the Name of that unreachable Prabhu whom the senses cannot reach.
The Gurmukh meditates on the Inaccessible, Unfathomable Lord. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to the True Guru, the True Primal Being.
By Guru's grace, I meditate on the Unapproachable and Unapprehensible God. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to my True Guru, the embodiment of the True Lord.
Through the True Guru I have meditated on Vahiguru, unreachable and beyond mind, speech and the senses. So I am a sacrifice, in mind and word, to that True Guru, the (sat) most exalted Being.
QVGE: Merai pran = in my life, in my every breath. Paras = touching. Naam = in the Name. ||1||
The Guru has made Parmatma's Name dwell in my every breath. Touching (the feet of) the Guru, I stay merged in Parmatma's Name. ||1||
He has brought the Lord's Name to dwell upon my breath of life; meeting with the True Guru, I am absorbed into the Lord's Name. ||1||
He has enshrined the Lord's Name within my vital breath. Meeting with the True Guru, I am absorbed in the Lord's Name.

He who gave me Ram's Name has settled my life-breath — that is, kept it from leaving me in separation; or it has come under control, meaning I hold it back and worship with every breath. Meeting (paras) that True Guru, I have merged into Hari's Name. ||1||
68R5: Tek = support. Tikaeea = has set up, has made.
O brother! (The Guru) has made Parmatma's Name the support (of the life) of (me,) His servant.
The Name of the Lord is the only Support of His humble servants.
God's Name is the only support of His slaves.
I, the servant, have (tikaeea) settled in — that is, taken — the (tek) shelter of Hari's Name.
FVWA: Dhar = support. Java = I go, I walk (on life's path). Dhar laaga = holding on. Te = from, through. Laheeaa = have found. ||1|| Rahau ||
Holding on to the Guru's hem, I walk on (the path of life); by the Guru's grace I have found the door (of the palace) of Parmatma. ||1|| Rahau ||
I shall live under the protection of the True Guru. By Guru's Grace, I shall attain the Court of the Lord. ||1||Pause||
I shall continue to abide under the True Guru's protection, By Guru's grace, I shall attain to the Lord's Court. Pause.
I go on, held in the (dhar) support and shelter of the True Guru. By the Guru's grace I have (laheeaa) found Hari's door. ||1|| Rahau ||
MY6R: Math = churning, refining. Tat = butter, high spiritual life.

O brother! This (human) body is (such a) field that deeds (as seeds, done day by day) are being sown in it. (Just as) butter is drawn out by churning and churning milk, (so,) taking the Guru's shelter (and refining and refining these daily deeds, one gains high spiritual life).
This body is the field of karma; the Gurmukhs plow and work it, and harvest the essence.
This body is the field to sow the seed of deeds. By churning and toiling, the pious persons gather essence.

This body is the field for sowing the seed of deeds; but the Gurmukhs, having gained this body, (math math) plough it — that is, by practice and reflection again and again — and draw out the essence, the grain: what is it? the essence of the self. Or this line has two illustrations, the field and milk: churning with the churn of reflection they draw out the butter of the essence.
FPVH: Pragasia = has made shine (by the Guru), has brought to light. Bhandai tit = in that (heart-)vessel. Bhau = love. Aeea = has come in. ||2||
(In whatever heart-vessel the Guru) brings to light the greatly precious Name (of Parmatma), love comes to dwell in that (heart-)vessel. ||2||
The priceless jewel of the Naam becomes manifest, and it pours into their vessels of love. ||2||
The invaluable jewel of the Name becomes manifest and it pours into their vessel of love.
Vahiguru's Name shines like rubies and jewels; in whichever vessel of the heart there is (bhau) love, the Name comes into it — meaning it settles there. ||2||
Q16Y: Hoe = becoming. Raheeai = one should stay. Jo jan = the people who. Nij = His own special.
O brother! Those who (taking the Guru's shelter) become Parmatma's own special devotees — one should live as the servant of the servants of their servants.
Become the slave of the slave of the slave, of that humble being who has become the devotee of the Lord.
The person, who has become the Lord's own servant; Be you the slave of the slave of his slave.
So, O (bhaeea) brother! Those who are Ram's own devotees — let us become, in mind, body and speech, the servants of their servants.
PH85: Arap = offering. Dharau = I place. Parsadi = by the grace alone. Akath = whose true form cannot be told. Kathaeea = I am praising. ||3||
I have offered (my) mind before (my) Guru; I have offered my intellect. By the Guru's grace alone I praise that Parmatma whose true form cannot be told. ||3||
I dedicate my mind and intellect, and place them in offering before my Guru; by Guru's Grace, I speak the Unspoken. ||3||
Dedicating my soul and intellect, I place them before the Guru. By Guru's grace I utter the Unutterable One.
Offer mind, body and understanding wholly and place them before that True Guru, by whose grace I have spoken the praise of (akath) Vahiguru. ||3||
AXLW: Manmukh = people who follow their own mind. Moh = in attachment. Viape = stay caught. Tikhaeea = thirst, craving.
O brother! People who follow their own mind stay (always) caught in attachment to Maya; this mind (of theirs) keeps burning in the craving (for Maya).
The self-willed manmukhs are engrossed in attachment to Maya; their minds are thirsty, burning with desire.
The way-ward are engrossed in the love of worldly valuables. Their soul is thirsty and burns in desire.
The self-willed are caught in the attachment of Maya; so this mind of theirs, burning with craving, stays parched — meaning it is made wretched by craving.
3TCJ: Amrit jal = water that gives spiritual life. Agan = the fire (of craving). Gur sabad = by the Guru's Word. ||4||
(The person who,) taking the Guru's teaching, found the water of the Name that gives spiritual life — (the) fire (of craving within them) was put out; the Guru's Word put it out. ||4||
Following the Guru's Teachings, I have obtained the Ambrosial Water of the Naam, and the fire has been put out. The Word of the Guru's Shabad has put it out. ||4||
By Guru's instruction I have received the ambrosial water of the Lord's Name and my fire is quenched. The Transcendent Name has quenched it.
Those who, taking the Guru's teaching, have found the nectar-water of the Name — their fire, put out by the Guru's Word, has been put out. ||4||
VT04: Naachai = dances. Naachai satgur aagai = dances before the Guru, walks wherever the Guru leads {ordinarily a person keeps dancing in Maya's hands}. Anhad = {anahata} sounding without being played, unbroken, continuous. Dhun = current. Toor = instruments.
O brother! (The person whose) mind walks wherever the Guru leads — (within them) the instruments of the current of the Bani of praise keep playing (as it were) unbroken.
This mind dances before the True Guru. The unstruck sound current of the Shabad resounds, vibrating the celestial melody.
This soul of mine dances before the True Guru and within me resounds the Tune of the celestial music of the Name.
When this mind dances the dance of devotion before the True Guru, then (anhad) unbroken, the (toor) instrument of Hari's praise plays — fixing the (dhun) attention in the Guru's Word, or speaking it.

0V2B: Ustat = praise. Charan har = Hari's feet. Rakh rakh = placing again and again, placing at every moment. {Note: instruments are played along with one who dances in rhythm. Walking in the Guru's will is the dancing. The unbroken love for the Bani of praise is the instruments. Keeping Prabhu's remembrance in the mind at every moment is stepping in rhythm.} ||5||
That person keeps praising Parmatma day and night, at every moment; keeping Prabhu's feet always (in the heart), (that person) keeps (the steps of life) in rhythm. ||5||
I praise the Lord, day and night, moving my feet to the beat of the drum. ||5||
Placing, placing my feet with the beating of time, day and night sing I the praise of the Lord Master God.

In every way they praise Hari day and night. Placing their feet again and again — that is, holding back the senses again and again — they keep the rhythm before Hari, meaning they hold the mind still in the true form. ||5||
EPBN: Kai rang = in the (love-)colour of. Rata = dyed. Ras = with delight. Rasal = {ras-alaya} Prabhu, the source of all delights. Rasal ras = in Parmatma's love. Ravia = keeps enshrined in the heart.

O brother! (The person whose) mind, dyed in the (love-)colour of Prabhu, keeps singing (songs of praise), (who) keeps chanting the Guru's Word with delight in the love of Prabhu, the source of delights —
Imbued with the Lord's Love, my mind sings His Praise, joyfully chanting the Shabad, the source of nectar and bliss.
Imbued with God's love, my soul sings His praise and joyfully utters the Name of the Home of Nectar and bliss.

The mind dyed in the (rang) love of Hari sings the virtues of that Vahiguru. Now, through the Guru's (sabad) teaching, we delight in the (rasal) finest delight among delights — meaning we are absorbed in that bliss.
KT7J: Nij ghar = in one's own (heart-)home. Chuai = keeps trickling. Ati = very. Jin = which (person). Tin hi = {the 'i' of 'tini' drops because of the adverb 'hi'} that one alone. ||6||
— in that person's heart a very pure stream (of the life-giving water of the Name) keeps trickling. The person who has drunk (this water of the Name) alone has gained spiritual bliss. ||6||
The stream of immaculate purity flows through the home of the self within; one who drinks it in, finds peace. ||6||
Within one's own home trickles the supremely immaculate stream, He who drink it attains to peace.

In our own home, the heart, a stream of nectar, the bliss of the self, very pure, has (chuai) come to us. And others too who have drunk this nectar of the bliss of the self — they alone have (laheeaa) found everything. ||6||
ADMD: Man hath = through the stubbornness of the mind. Karam = (prescribed religious) deeds. Abhimani = proud. Baloo = sand.
(The person who) keeps doing (prescribed religious) deeds through the stubbornness (of their) mind becomes proud (of being religious); (their efforts are then) like children building houses of sand.
The stubborn-minded, egotistical, proud-minded person performs rituals, but these are like sand castles built by children.
Through his mind's obstinacy, the proud man performs rituals, but these are like house of sand built by a child.
Without the Guru, the deeds this proud being does through stubbornness of mind are like a child building a house of (baloo) sand on the seashore.
LAL7: A wave of the sea's water comes, and those houses collapse in an instant, grain by grain. ||7||
When the waves of the ocean come in, they crumble and dissolve in an instant. ||7||
When the waves of the vast ocean dash against it, in an instant, it crumbles into pieces and bits.

When a wave of water comes from the ocean made by the sons of (sagar) Sagar, in that instant the house of sand falls apart, bit by bit. In the same way, with the wave that is the using up of merit, the pleasures that are the fruit of deeds done for reward are destroyed. ||7|| ☬ Now, with the illustration of waves, he shows the oneness of the world with Brahm:
JENF: Sar = lake, pool. Sagar = ocean. Aape = Himself. Sabh = all.
O brother! This whole world is a play (Parmatma) has staged; He Himself is the lake (of life), the ocean (and all beings are waves of that ocean).
The Lord is the pool, and the Lord Himself is the ocean; this world is all a play which He has staged.
God is the pool and God Himself is the ocean, this world is all a play staged by Him.
Hari Himself is in every way like the ocean. This world is all His play — the waves He has played out, or spread out.
VX6H: Tarang = waves. Jalah = in the water itself {jalah = jal hi; the 'i' of 'jali' drops because of the adverb 'hi'}. Samavah = merge. ||8||3||6||
O Nanak! Just as the waves of (the sea's) water (are the sea's) water (itself) and merge back into the water, (so) that beautiful Ram is Himself, Himself alone (everywhere). ||8||3||6||
As the waves of water merge into the water again, O Nanak, so does He merge into Himself. ||8||3||6||
As the water of the sea waves merges in the sea, so, O Nanak, the omnipresent Lord is all by the Himself.

Just as, when waves seem separate from the water, they are still the very form of water; and when those waves (samavah) cease in the water, they merge in the water and become water — Sri Guru ji says: so now too, the form of all is Ramaeea Himself alone, and when the waves that are bodies cease, Brahm alone will remain. Meaning: form is imagined, and what is imagined has no being apart from its ground. ||8||3||6|| ☬ Rejecting hypocrisy without love of the True One, he teaches his own mind:
CVW7: Parchai = is pleased (with whom). Man = in the mind. Tan = on the body. Bhasam = ashes. Drirraeea = made firmly settled in the heart.

O brother! (Those people with whom) the Guru is pleased (have, as it were, worn the yogi's) earrings in (their) mind (this pleasure of the Guru); (they) have firmly settled the Guru's Word (in their heart — this is the) ash smeared on (their) body.
My mind wears the ear-rings of the True Guru's acquaintance; I apply the ashes of the Word of the Guru's Shabad to my body.
My mind wears the rings of the union with True Guru and I apply the ashes of the Guru's instruction to my body.
O mind! Those who have worn the pair of earrings of being absorbed in the True Guru's teaching, and have firmly smeared the (bhasam) ash of the Guru's Word alone on the body —
Q4CE: Amar = deathless. Pind = body. Amar pind = with deathless bodies, freed from the round of birth and death. Sadhu sang = in the Guru's company. Dou = both. ||1||
(In this way) living in the Guru's company they have escaped the round of birth and death; their birth and death have both come to an end. ||1||
My body has become immortal, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy. Both birth and death have come to an end for me. ||1||
My being has become eternal in the society of the saints and ended are both my births and deaths.
those people, through the company of the saints, have become (amar pind) deathless in form, and both their birth and death have been wiped away. ||1||
QGK0: O my mind! One should live joined to the Guru's company (and keep praying):
O my mind, remain united with the Saadh Sangat.
O my soul!, remain you ever united with the society of saints.
O my mind! Stay joined to the company of the saints.
VK0H: Madh soodan = O Madhusudan! O slayer of the demon Madhu! Madhau = O Master of Maya! (dhav = husband). Pakhaeea = may I keep washing. ||1|| Rahau ||
O Madhusudan! O Madho! Show (me) mercy, that I may keep washing the Guru's feet at every moment (stay in the Guru's shelter at every moment). ||1|| Rahau ||
Be merciful to me, O Lord; each and every instant, let me wash the Feet of the Holy. ||1||Pause||
O God, the Destroyer of Madh demon and the Lord of wealth, show mercy to me, so that every moment I wash the saints feet. Pause.

Pray like this: O Madho, (soodan) destroyer of demons such as Madhu and Kaitabh! Show me such grace that at every instant I may (pakhaeea) wash the feet of the saints, or keep beholding them. ||1|| Rahau || ☬ Now he tells the state of those who are not absorbed in the True Guru's Word:
4K36: Tajai = gives up, leaves. Banvasi = dweller in the forest.
But, O brother! (The person who) leaves household life and goes to live in the forest — (in this way their) mind does not settle for even an instant, however much they try to settle it.
Forsaking family life, he wanders in the forest, but his mind does not remain at rest, even for an instant.
Renouncing family life, man becomes a forest-dweller, but his mind remains not at rest, even for a moment.
The person who, without love of the Name, gives up household life and even comes to live in the forests — their mind, though held down, does not stay still for even an instant.
YLEQ: Dhavat = the wandering mind. Dhai = wandering, running. Tade = only then. Ghar = in the home. Sadhu = the Guru. ||2||
O brother! This wandering mind, after wandering and wandering, comes to rest only when a person takes the shelter of Parmatma, of the Guru. ||2||
The wandering mind returns home, only when it seeks the Sanctuary of the Lord's Holy people. ||2||
Then alone the wandering soul returns home, when it seeks the refuge of the Lord God's saints.

This mind, which runs after (dhavat) perishable things, only then comes (ghar) home to the true form and becomes one-pointed, when, falling at the shelter of the saints, it chants the Name Har Har. ||2||
ZRC8: Chhod = leaving. Man = in the mind.
O brother! (The person who) leaves daughters and sons (family) and becomes a sannyasi (still) keeps building countless hopes in (their) mind,
The Sannyaasi renounces his daughters and sons, but his mind still conjures up all sorts of hopes and desires.
Even an anchoret, who abandons his daughters and sons, conceives many desires within his mind.
Though they left daughters and sons and even became a sannyasi, still their mind kept hoping and hoping greatly.
70MN: Karai = does. Boojhai = understands. Kai sabad = through the Word of. Niras = free of hope. ||3||
keeps building hopes every day (and so) does not understand (true spiritual life). But yes! Through the Guru's Word, rising above the hopes of the world, a person can enjoy spiritual bliss. ||3||
With these hopes and desires, he still does not understand, that only through the Word of the Guru's Shabad does one become free of desires, and find peace. ||3||
He entertains desires upon desires and understands not, that by Guru's instruction alone, man is freed from desires and obtains peace.

They go about hoping and hoping. This being does not (boojhai) understand the Guru's Word, through whose support the peace of being free of hope is (laheeaa) found — meaning the bliss of Brahm is found. ||3||
HK27: Tarak = disgust. Digambar = {dig-ambar; dig = direction; ambar = cloth} one who has made the four directions their clothing, naked, a Jain. Dah dis = in the ten directions. Chal chal = going and going, wandering and wandering. Gavan = roaming, running about.
O brother! (There is someone in whose mind) disgust (for the world) arises; they become a naked sadhu; (yet their) mind keeps running and wandering in the ten directions,
When detachment from the world wells up within, he become a naked hermit, but still, his mind roams, wanders and rambles in the ten directions.
When detachment from the world wells up in man, he becomes a naked hermit, but his mind roams rambles and flees in ten directions.

When, through separation from wife, sons and others, disgust arose in the heart, then they gave up household life and became (digambar) naked. They even took on such a garb, but their mind, (chal) like a spinning top, (chal) restless, roams in the ten directions — meaning it makes plans to get the things of the ten directions.
54TF: Prabhavan = roaming (the whole land). Mil = joining. Daia ghar = the home of mercy, Hari the source of mercy. ||4||
(That person) goes roaming (the earth); (their) craving (for Maya still) does not go. But yes, joining the Guru's company, a person finds Parmatma, the source of mercy. ||4||
He wanders around, but his desires are not satisfied; joining the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, he finds the house of kindness and compassion. ||4||
He wanders about, but his desire is quenched not. Meeting with the society of the saints he obtains the House of mercy.
In this way they (prabhavan) roam about greatly, but the fire of craving is not put out. So when one joins the company of the saints, then through their mercy one sees the (ghar) true self. ||4||
MCJZ: Sidh = siddhas, yogis perfected (in yogic practice). Sikhah = learn. Man = in the mind. Maagah = ask for. Ridh sidh = miraculous powers. Chetak = miraculous shows.

O brother! Yogis perfected (in yogic practice) learn many postures {such as the headstand and the lotus posture}, but they too keep asking in their mind for miraculous powers and shows (with which to impress ordinary people).
The Siddhas learn many Yogis postures, but their minds still yearn for riches, miraculous powers and energy.
The Yogis learn many sitting postures, but their minds long for riches, miraculous powers and sorcery.
Many learn the many postures of the siddhas. Such people, becoming (chetakaeea) spell-casters, ask in their mind for miraculous powers for their shows, or to bring people under their sway.
J43N: Tripat = fulfilment (from Maya). Man = in the mind. Mil sadhu = meeting the Guru. Sidh = success. ||5||

(Their) mind finds no fulfilment from Maya; they gain no contentment; peace does not come into the mind. But yes, meeting the Guru, through Parmatma's Name a person gains fulfilment and gains the success of spiritual life. ||5||
Satisfaction, contentment and tranquility do not come to their minds; but meeting the Holy Saints, they are satisfied, and through the Name of the Lord, spiritual perfection is attained. ||5||
Satiation, contentment and peace enter not man's mind By meeting the saints, man is sated and by God's Name, he procures perfection.

The peace that would come from fulfilment through contentment does not come into the mind. Those who, meeting the saints, have gained the success of Hari's Name — or purity of heart, or liberation — they alone, being fulfilled, have found peace. ||5|| ☬ He speaks of the greatness of the company of the saints and the shelter of Parmeshar:
E7B7: Andaj = born from eggs. Jeraj = born from the womb. Setaj = born from sweat. Utbhuj = {udbhijja} sprouting from the earth. Sabh = all. Varan = colours.
O brother! Those born from eggs, those born from the womb, those born from sweat, those sprouting from the earth — all these beings and creatures of countless forms and colours Parmatma has created.
Life is born from the egg, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth; God created the beings and creatures of all colors and forms.
Egg-born, foetus-born, sweat-born, earth-born, the mortals and the creatures of all the colours and forms are made by God.
Beings with gross bodies and colours, and subtle creatures, in these four sources — from eggs, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth — all were created by Vahiguru.
B29P: (Among these, the being who) comes to the Guru's shelter escapes (from the world-ocean), whether they are a Kshatriya or a Brahmin, a Shudra or a Vaishya, or the lowest outcaste. ||6||
One who seeks the Sanctuary of the Holy is saved, whether he is a Kh'shaatriya, a Brahmin, a Soodra, a Vaishya or the most untouchable of the untouchables. ||6||
He who takes saints' protection is saved, be he a warrior, a literate, an agriculturist and untouchable and the pariah of the pariahs.

Among these, whoever falls at the shelter of the saints is saved from suffering: Kshatriya, Brahmin, Shudra, Vaishya — the four castes — and the outcaste, and (chandaeea) the one who does the lowest work among outcastes. Meaning: all who are exalted, and the lowest of the low, are saved by falling at the shelter of the saints. ||6|| ☬ If anyone asks who has been saved, he says:
3C48: O brother! Namdev, Jaidev, Kabir, Trilochan, Ravidas the cobbler of low caste,
Naam Dayv, Jai Dayv, Kabeer, Trilochan and Ravi Daas the low-caste leather-worker,
Namdev, Jaidev, Kabir, Tirlochan and Ravidas, tanner of low caste swam across.
Namdev ji and Jaidev ji, Kabir, then Trilochan ji, and Ravidas ji, a cobbler by caste, (chamaeea) who worked in leather,
23FN: Sadhu jan sangat = in the company of the saints. Dhan = blessed, fortunate. Daeea = Prabhu, the home of mercy. ||7||
Dhanna the Jat, Sain (the barber) — whoever joined the company of the saints became fortunate and met Parmatma, the source of mercy. ||7||
blessed Dhanna and Sain; all those who joined the humble Saadh Sangat, met the Merciful Lord. ||7||
Blessed Dhanna Jat, Sain and all those, who joined the society of the pious persons, did meet the Merciful Master.

— and so on: whoever, high or low, has joined the company of the saints has become the very form of well-being. And blessed is Dhanna the devotee, a Jat by caste, and Sain the devotee. By keeping the true company, all of these have met Hari, the inner mover of all. ||7||
QPDW: Paij = honour. Bhagat vachhal = Hari, who loves devotion. Angeekar = the side one takes.
(O brother!) Parmatma loves devotion; He has always kept the honour of His saints and always taken the side of His saints.
The Lord protects the honor of His humble servants; He is the Lover of His devotees - He makes them His own.
God the Lover of devotion, protects the honour of the saintly persons and accepts them.
That Hari Himself, through devotion, has kept the (paij) pledge, or honour, of such saints of His. That Vahiguru, the (vachhal) beloved of devotees, takes the (angeekar) side of His servants.
HL7X: Saran jag jeevan = the shelter of Prabhu, the life of the world. Rakhaeea = protects. ||8||4||7||
O Nanak! (Say:) those who take the shelter of Prabhu, the life of the world — Prabhu, in His grace, protects them. ||8||4||7||
Nanak has entered the Sanctuary of the Lord, the Life of the world, who has showered His Mercy upon him, and saved him. ||8||||4||7||
Nanak has entered the sanctuary of the Lord God, the life of the world and has mercifully emancipated him.

Sri Guru ji says: those who have thus fallen at the shelter of Vahiguru, the form of the life of the world — that is, who gives it being and vitality — Hari, showing grace, has given them His Name and saved them from the world-ocean. ||8||4||7|| ☬ Showing the love in his mind, he tells his own state:
B0MM: Antar = within (me). Pias = longing. Prabh keri = for (meeting) Prabhu. Sun = hearing. Man = in (my) mind.
O brother! Hearing the Guru's words, (it is as if) arrows (of separation) have struck (my) mind; a longing for a sight of Prabhu has arisen within me.
The thirst for God has welled up deep within me; hearing the Word of the Guru's Teachings, my mind is pierced by His arrow.
Within me, thirst for the Lord has welled up and hearing the Guru's word my soul is pierced through with an arrow,
When, hearing the Guru's words, the arrow of love struck my mind, then the thirst for a sight of Prabhu arose within me.

4LR3: Birha = pain. Man hi = the mind alone {the (ੁ) of 'manu' drops because of the adverb 'hi'}. Jaanai = knows. Avar ko = anyone else. Ki = what? Paraeea = another's. ||1||
O brother! Only (my own) mind knows the pain of (my) mind (at this time). What can anyone else know of another's pain? ||1||
The pain of my mind is known only to my own mind; who can know the pain of another? ||1||
The pain of my mind is known to my kind alone who else can know the pain of another?
The mind alone knows the (birtha) pain of that mind; who else can know another's pain? That is, no one else can know it. ||1||
X9Q2: Ram = O (my) Ram! Gur = by the Guru. Mohan = by the Enchanter. Gur mohan = by the enchanting Guru, by the beloved Guru. Moh laeea = has enchanted, has brought under His sway.
O (my) Ram! The beloved Guru has brought (my) mind under His sway.
The Lord, the Guru, the Enticer, has enticed my mind.
The Guru-God, the bewitcher, has bewitched my soul,
(Ram) O brother! The True Guru, the Enchanter, has enchanted my mind.
D4VG: Hau = I. Aakal bikal = {akula, vikala = disturbed, unnerved} distraught. Aakal bikal bhaee = I have lost my cleverness and wisdom. Lot pot = out of control, beyond my own mind's control. ||1|| Rahau ||
Seeing the Guru, I have (now) lost my cleverness and wisdom; I am no longer in my own control (my mind and my senses have come under the Guru's sway). ||1|| Rahau ||
I am stunned and amazed, gazing upon my Guru; I have entered the realm of wonder and bliss. ||1||Pause||
Seeing my Guru I am wonder-struck and I have entered the realm of beatitude. Pause.
I, who had my wits, have become (bikal) senseless from seeing the Guru. By that, turning away from the world, I have fallen senseless, rolling in love. ||1|| Rahau ||
18TZ: Nirkhat phirau = I go about searching. Sabh = all. Disantar = other lands. Ko = of. Man = in (my) mind. Chaeea = eagerness.
O brother! A great eagerness to see Prabhu has arisen in (my) mind; I go (went) searching (for Him) through all lands and countries.
I wander around, exploring all lands and foreign countries; within my mind, I have such a great longing to see my God.
I go about seeing all the country and foreign lands, as within my mind, there is a great yearning to see my Lord.
So I go about looking through all lands and countries, because a very great (chaeea) eagerness to see Prabhu has arisen in my mind.
ZSYN: Kaat = cutting. Deu = I give. Jin = which (Guru). Maarag = path. Panth = way. Dikhaeea = has shown. ||2||
The (Guru) who has shown (me) the way (to union with) Prabhu — before that Guru I am cutting and offering my body (giving myself over to the Guru). ||2||
I sacrifice my mind and body to the Guru, who has shown me the Way, the Path to my Lord God. ||2||
Sacrifice I my soul and body to the Guru, who has shown me the path and way to my God Lord.
He who, out of the ways of the world, has shown me the path to Hari Prabhu — before that True Guru I would cut and give my mind and body; that is, break from the world, or give up pride. ||2||
BP3N: Aan sadesa = bringing a message. Dei = gives. Kera = of. Rid antar = in the heart. Man = in the mind. Tan = in the body. Lagaeea = feels.
O brother! (Now if) anyone brings a message of Prabhu and gives it (to me), it feels sweet in my heart, my mind and my body.
If only someone would bring me news of God; He seems so sweet to my heart, mind and body.
If some one brings to me the message of my Lord, to my mind, heart and body, he seems sweet.
If anyone even comes and gives me a message of Prabhu — that is, recites the words of the Veda through which Parmeshar the Husband is reached — it feels supremely sweet in my heart, mind and body.
R58N: Mastak = forehead, head. Kaat = cutting. Deu = I give. Tal = beneath. ||3||
O brother! Whatever friend unites me with Prabhu — I am ready to cut off my head and place it beneath their feet. ||3||
I would cut off my head and place it under the feet of that one who leads me to meet and unite with my Lord God. ||3||
Chopping off my head, I would place it under the feet of him, who makes me meet my God Lord and unites me with His guild.
I would cut off my own head and place it beneath the feet of the Guru — that is, give up pride — who, joining me to the company of the true, would unite Hari Prabhu with me. ||3||
VGN1: Chal = come, let's go. Sakhi = O companion! Prabh parbodhah = let us awaken, stir, shake (the love of) Prabhu. Kaman = charms, the songs girls sing to win over the bridegroom when the wedding party arrives. Kar = making. Laheeaa = let us find.
O companion! Come, let's go; O companion! Come, let's go; let us (go and) stir (the love of) Prabhu; with the charms of (spiritual) virtues let us win over that Husband-Prabhu.
Let us go, O my companions, and understand our God; with the spell of virtue, let us obtain our Lord God.
O my mates, let us go and under stand our Lord and practising the charm of virtues, obtain our Lords Master.

O companions, the saints! Walking His path with mind and speech, let you and me (prabodhah) come to know Prabhu's form especially — or (prabodhah) win Him over, that is, please Him. For by the (kaman) charm of taking on virtues, that Hari Prabhu is found.
DNCG: Bhagat vachhal = loving devotion. Kaheeat = is called. Ua ko = His. ||4||
"Lover of devotion" — this is said to be His Name; (O companion, come,) let us take His shelter, let us fall at His door. ||4||
He is called the Lover of His devotees; let us follow in the footsteps of those who seek God's Sanctuary. ||4||
He goes by the Name of the lover of His saints. Let us follow the footstep of those, l who sought the Lord's refuge.
"Beloved of devotees" is said to be Vahiguru's Name; so the saints who have fallen at Prabhu's shelter — I too have fallen in behind them. Meaning, let us take the support of that true company. ||4||
BHEP: Khima = the nature that bears others' wrongs. Seegar = adornment. Man = in the mind. Deepak = lamp. Giaan = understanding of spiritual life. Balaeea = lights.
O companion! The soul-bride who makes a forgiving nature the adornment of her spiritual life, who lights in her mind the lamp of the understanding of spiritual life received from the Guru —
If the soul-bride adorns herself with compassion and forgiveness, God is pleased, and her mind is illumined with the lamp of the Guru's wisdom.
If the bride adorns herself with compassion, my Lord is pleased with her and the lamp of Guru's wisdom is kindles within her mind.
So when the soul-bride, the seeker, puts on the adornment of forgiveness, then Prabhu is (aa) especially pleased, and through the Guru the lamp of knowledge (balaeea) shines in the mind.
MS70: Ras ras = with great delight. Bhog karai = enjoys union. Jeeo = life. Kat kat = cutting again and again. ||5||
— the Husband-Prabhu is pleased with her. Prabhu enjoys spiritual union with her in great bliss. O companion! I am ready to offer my life again and again before that Husband-Prabhu. ||5||
With happiness and ecstasy, my God enjoys her; I offer each and every bit of my soul to Him. ||5||
With gladness and glee, My Lord enjoy her, To that Lord of Mine, I offer every bit of my body.
Those with whom my Prabhu, (ras) in love, (ras) one with them, enjoys union — meaning makes them one with Himself — before that person we lay down our life, cutting it again and again. ||5||
2TJ0: Kanth = at the neck. Moteechoor = an ornament for the head. Gahan = ornaments.

O companion! I have put on my neck the necklace of Parmatma's Name (remembered with every breath); I have made (my own) mind (made beautiful through remembrance) the greatest ornament, the moteechoor.
I have made the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, my necklace; my mind tinged with devotion is the intricate ornament of crowning glory.
The Lord's name, I have made my Necklace and the love-filled mind is the supreme ornament for my head decoration.

The necklace of the Name Har Har is made and shines at their neck. And (gahan) seizing the mind, (choor) crushing its false nature, they have made it pure as a pearl. This purified mind is the great ornament — meaning, bringing the mind under control is to wear a great jewel.
ZWAK: Man = in the mind. Bhaeea = feels dear. ||6||
I have spread the bed of faith in Hari's Name (in my heart); that Husband-Prabhu feels very dear in my mind (now I am sure that) the Husband-Prabhu cannot leave me. ||6||
I have spread out my bed of faith in the Lord, Har, Har. I cannot abandon Him - my mind is filled with such a great love for Him. ||6||
For my Lord Master I have spread the bedding of faith. I can abandon not my Lord, as within my mind there is immense affection for Him.
To reach that Hari Prabhu, one has spread in every way the bed of faith in the mind and heart; then that bed pleases Prabhu, and so He cannot leave it. ||6||
9WRE: Keejai = one keeps doing. Sabh seegar = all adornment. Phokat = empty, useless.

O companion! (If) the Husband-Prabhu keeps saying one thing and (the soul-bride) keeps doing another, then all (that soul-bride's) adornment (all her religious effort) goes to waste and becomes utterly empty.
If God says one thing, and the soul-bride does something else, then all her decorations are useless and false.
If the Lord says one thing and the bride does quite another, then vain and refuse-like are all her decorations.
If Prabhu says one thing and we do another — that is, do not obey Vahiguru's command — then all the adornment of good virtues is useless and (phokat phokataeea) utterly fruitless.
4Y5J: Milan kai taai = in order to meet. Leeo suhagan = made the happy bride His own. Mukh = on the face (of the one who only adorns herself). ||7||
(On her) face there is only spitting; that Prabhu has made (some other) happy bride His own. ||7||
She may adorn herself to meet her Husband Lord, but still, only the virtuous soul-bride meets God, and the other's face is spat upon. ||7||
The bride bedecks herself to meet with her Spouse, but the chaste brides obtain the Lord and her face is spat at.
The happy brides who put on the adornment of all virtues to meet Prabhu have found Prabhu. And the unhappy ones who do not obey the command get spat upon — meaning they meet only scorn. ||7||
Q975: Cheri = handmaidens, servants. Agam = unreachable. Gusai = Master of the earth. Kia ham karah = what can we do? Terai vas = under Your control.
O Prabhu! We are Your handmaidens; You are unreachable, the Master of the earth. We soul-brides can do nothing (outside Your command); we are always under Your control.
I am Your hand-maiden, O Inaccessible Lord of the Universe; what can I do by myself? I am under Your power.
I am a hand-maiden of Yours. You are the infinite Lord of the universe, I am under Your sway. What can I of myself do?

So let the seeker pray before that Vahiguru like this: O You, unreachable by mind and speech! You are my Master and I am Your (cheri) handmaiden. I am in Your power; so what can I do without You? That is, I can do nothing.
DHDL: O Nanak! (Say:) O Hari! Show mercy to us poor ones; keep us at Your feet; keep us merged in the Guru's shelter. ||8||5||8||
Be merciful, Lord, to the meek, and save them; Nanak has entered the Sanctuary of the Lord, and the Guru. ||8||5||8||
O Lord, show You mercy to the meek ones and save them. Nanak has entered into Yours sanctuary, O Guru-God.

So, O Prabhu! Show mercy to me, the humble, and save me from the sufferings of the world. Sri Guru ji says: O Hari, (gur) greater than all! We beings find our resting place in Your shelter alone. ||8||5||8|| ☬ Again, with eagerness, he teaches in his own words:
ZLNV: Mai man = in my mind. Mai tan = in my body. Agam = unreachable. Sardha = longing.
O companion! In my mind and in my body love for the unreachable Master Prabhu has arisen; again and again a burning longing for union with Him is arising in my mind.
My mind and body are filled with love for my Inaccessible Lord and Master. Each and every instant, I am filled with immense faith and devotion.
Within my mind and body is the love of the infinite Lord. Every instant immense faith wells up in my mind.
Love for that unreachable Thakur has come into my mind and body. From that, at every instant, ever greater faith rises in my mind.
J62X: Sardha man = the longing of the mind. Chatrik mukh = in the rainbird's mouth. ||1||
O companion! Seeing the Guru, this longing of the mind is fulfilled, as (a) drop (of rain) falls into the mouth of the rainbird crying "Priu, priu". ||1||
Gazing upon the Guru, my mind's faith is fulfilled, like the song-bird, which cries and cries, until the rain-drop falls into its mouth. ||1||
Seeing the Guru, my mind's yearning is fulfilled, as the pied-cuckoo is pacified, when after plaintive cry, the rain.-drop falls into its mouth.

Seeing the True Guru, the faith of my mind has been fulfilled. As the (chatrik) rainbird cries "priu priu" for the svati drop, and when the svati drop falls into its mouth it finds peace — so I, like the rainbird, longed for the drop of teaching. When the True Guru gave the nectar-drop of the teaching of the Name, then my mind found peace. ||1||
BFH4: Sakhi = O companion! Katha = praise. Sunaeea = let us hear.
O companion! Come, let us sit together, let us sit together, (and, sitting) hear Parmatma's praise.
Join with me, join with me, O my companions, and teach me the Sermon of the Lord.
Meet, meet me, O my mates and utter to me the Lord's discourse.
O brother! Meeting again and again with the saints, our companions, we hear the story of that Hari.
YQZN: Mele = unites. Mai sir = my head. Paeea = is laid. ||1|| Rahau ||
The one on whom the Guru shows mercy, He unites (with) Prabhu. Before that (Guru) my head is offered again and again. ||1|| Rahau ||
The True Guru has mercifully united me with God. Cutting off my head, and chopping it into pieces, I offer it to Him. ||1||Pause||
The True Guru has mercifully united me with my Lord. Chopping, chopping off, my head, I offer it to him. Pause.
When I cut off my head and lay it before Him, then the True Guru, in mercy, will unite me with Prabhu. ||1|| Rahau ||
QL4C: Rom rom = in every pore. Bedan = the pain of separation.
O companion! In every pore of mine, in my mind and in my body there is (the) pain (of separation from Prabhu); without seeing Prabhu I find no peace.
Each and every hair on my head, and my mind and body, suffer the pains of separation; without seeing my God, I cannot sleep.
In every hair, mind and body of mine, is the pang of separation. Without seeing my Lord, I can sleep not.
In every pore of my mind and body is the (bedan) pain of separation from the One Vahiguru; so without seeing Prabhu I cannot sleep.
5WSQ: Baidak = physicians. Naatik = pulse. Dekh = seeing. Peer = pain. ||2||
The physicians go wrong (just) by feeling (my) pulse; in my heart, my mind and my body it is the pain of Prabhu's love that is rising. ||2||
The doctors and healers look at me, and are perplexed. Within my heart, mind and body, I feel the pain of divine love. ||2||
Seeing me, the physicians and the pulse-feelers are non-plussed. Within my soul, mind and body is the pain of the Lord's love.

The physicians who read the books of medicine go astray feeling the (naatik) pulse — meaning they cannot know this pain of love, and say they cannot find the disease. In my heart, in mind and body, the pain of love for that Master is gripping me. ||2||
2YV6: Hau = I. Sakau = I can. Amal = intoxicant. Amli = an addict.
O companion! As an addict comes close to death without the intoxicant, so I cannot live even an instant or a moment without union with the Beloved Prabhu.
I cannot live for a moment, for even an instant, without my Beloved, like the opium addict who cannot live without opium.
Even for an instant and trice, I can live not without my Beloved, as an opium-addict can live not without opium-addict can live not without opium.
I cannot live even an instant or a moment without that Beloved, just as an addict dies without taking the drug.
KS58: Pias = longing. Keri = for. Ko duia = any other. ||3||
O companion! The soul-brides who long for union with the Husband-Prabhu find no one else pleasing except Prabhu. ||3||
Those who thirst for God, do not love any other. Without the Lord, there is no other at all. ||3||
They, who feel thirst for the Lord; without God, they love not any other.
Those who thirst for a sight of Prabhu find no one else pleasing but Hari. ||3||
4C3W: Aan = coming. Vitahu = to. Ghum gaeea = I am a sacrifice.
O companion! If anyone would come and unite me with my beloved Prabhu, I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to them.
If only someone would come and unite me with God; I am devoted, dedicated, a sacrifice to him.
Let some one come and unite me with my Lord, I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice and devoted to him.
If anyone (aan) brings — or turns me back from the world of duality towards Him — and unites me with my Master, I am a sacrifice (vitahu) to them with mind, body and speech.
8J8T: O companion! When one takes the True Guru's shelter, the True Guru unites (with Prabhu) those separated through countless births. ||4||
After being separated from the Lord for countless incarnations, I am re-united with Him, entering the Sanctuary of the True, True, True Guru. ||4||
When the mortal enters the sanctuary of the True, True, True Guru, then meets he with the Lord after separation of many births.

When they have (sat) surely come into the shelter of the True Guru, the giver of the True Name, then the True Guru has united with the form of Hari (jan) people who had been separated for countless births. ||4||

1RF0: Sej = the bed of the heart. Mahal = dwelling. Manmukh = the soul-bride who follows her own mind. Bharmaeea = wanders.

O companion! (The soul-bride) has one bed of the heart, on which the Master Prabhu Himself dwells; but the soul-bride who follows her own mind cannot find (the Husband-Prabhu's) dwelling; she only wanders.
There is one bed for the soul-bride, and the same bed for God, her Lord and Master. The self-willed manmukh does not obtain the Mansion of the Lord's Presence; she wanders around, in limbo.
The same is the couch for the soul and the Spouse and the same is the Lord master of all. An apostate mounts not to his Master's mansion and wanders about.
There is one bed, the heart, and the one able Thakur (Prabhu) is seated on it. But this self-willed being does not find the (mahal) true form, and keeps wandering in the 84 lakh births.
EUBR: Karat = while doing. Aai = coming. Dheel = delay. ||5||
If she comes to the Guru's shelter crying "Guru, Guru", then Prabhu comes and meets her; there is not the slightest delay. ||5||
Uttering, "Guru, Guru", she seeks His Sanctuary; so God comes to meet her, without a moment's delay. ||5||
Uttering "Guru, Guru", If the mortal seeks his refuge, the Lord comes and meets him without a moment's delay.
If, speaking the Guru's Name, one comes to the shelter of the True Guru, then Prabhu comes and meets them; there is no (dheel) delay in that meeting. ||5||
LN6A: Kar = doing. Kar kar = doing again and again. Kiriachar = kiria-achar, ritual. Man = in the mind. Pakhand = show. Kapat = deceit, trickery.

But if someone (leaving the Guru's support and forgetting remembrance of Hari's Name) keeps doing (prescribed religious deeds such as pilgrimages) again and again and keeps increasing these rituals, then only the working of greed, trickery and show will stay in their mind (there will be no union with the Husband-Prabhu).
One may perform many rituals, but the mind is filled with hypocrisy, evil deeds and greed.
The mortal performs many rituals, but in his mind he has harboured hypocrisy, evil deeds and covetousness.
Doing ritual again and again, they have increased their (achar) observances; and there is hypocrisy in the mind, so out of greed they do deceitful deeds.
HZWX: Besua = a woman of the market. Kai ghar = in the house of. Tah pita naam = his father's name. Kia sadaeea = what can be said? ||6||
If a son is born in the house of a woman of the market, no name can be given for that son's father. ||6||
When a son is born in the house of a prostitute, who can tell the name of his father? ||6||
A son is born in the house of a prostitute, what can be said to be the Name of his father?
Just as a son born in a prostitute's house — what name can be given for his father? None. So that hypocritical, deceitful, greedy person has no Guru or Pir. ||6||
TYMF: Poorab janam = in a previous birth. Kar = having done. Aae = came (into human birth). Gur = by the Guru. Bhagat jamaeea = sowed (the seed of Parmatma's) devotion (within them).
O brother! (Those who) have come (into human birth now) having done (Parmatma's) devotion in a previous birth — the Guru has sown in them the seed of devotion at every moment.
Because of devotional worship in my past incarnations, I have been born into this life. The Guru has inspired me to worship the Lord, Har, Har, Har, Har.
By virtue of the worship done in past lives, I am born human, The Guru has installed in me the Lord, Lord, Lord's meditation.

Those who have come having done Hari's devotion in earlier births — now too the True Guru has given them the Name Har Har and merged into their hearts the devotion that takes away suffering; that is, has brought it forth.
E13N: Karte = while doing. Bhagat bhagat karte = doing devotion at every moment. Naam = in the Name. ||7||
When, remembering and remembering Hari's Name at every moment, they merged into Hari's Name, then, doing devotion at every moment, they found union with Parmatma. ||7||
Worshipping, worshipping Him with devotion, I found the Lord, and then I merged into the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, Har, Har. ||7||
When I merged in the Lord, Lord, Lord, 's Name, then serving and praising the Lord, I attained to Him.

When, serving the devotees — or doing devotion with mind and speech — they found Hari's Name, then, chanting Hari's Name Har Har, they merged into that Hari, the Named — that is, became one with Him. ||7||
CVVY: Prabh = by Prabhu. Aan = bringing. Aape = Himself. Ghol = dissolving. Ang = on the body.

(But, O brother! Doing Parmatma's devotion is not in a being's own power. This toil can be done only by Prabhu's grace. Doing Prabhu's devotion is, as it were, like grinding henna. A woman grinds the henna herself, rubs it herself, and applies it herself to her hands and feet. She herself makes the henna fit to be applied to her limbs.) Prabhu Himself, bringing (the being's mind to His feet) again and again, has had the henna (of devotion) ground (by the being); then He Himself, dissolving and dissolving that henna of devotion (making it colourful and full of love), has joined them to His feet.
God Himself came and ground the henna leaves into powder, and applied it to my body.
The Lord Himself brought and powdered the henna-leaves and Himself applied its paste to my body-limbs.

Bringing this mind (aan) towards Prabhu, away from duality — or (aan aan) turning the mind back again and again and making it subtle through spiritual practice — this is grinding the henna. Practising again and again is dissolving it, and He Himself has applied it (ang) to the heart; that is, He has settled the mind, made ready through practice, in the heart.
9KQT: Thakur = by the Master. Pakar = holding. ||8||6||2||1||6||9||
O Nanak! (Say: O brother!) Those on whom the Master Prabhu showed grace, He took by the arm and pulled out (of the world-ocean). ||8||6||2||1||6||9||
Our Lord and Master showers His Mercy upon us, and grasps hold of our arms; O Nanak, He lifts us up and saves us. ||8||6||9||2||1||6||9||
They, to whom the Lord extends His mercy, catching by the arm, He pulls them out of the world-ocean, O Nanak.

Those on whom Thakur ji has shown grace — Sri Guru ji says: He has taken them by the arm of understanding and pulled them out of the sufferings of the world. ||8||6||9|| ☬ He speaks of Vahiguru's virtues and the greatness of the Name:
